titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§208–210: Jürchedei, Ibaqa and the Four Dogs
part: §§208–210 — Jürchedei, Ibaqa and the Four Dogs
about: Chinggis continues the rewards of 1206. He recalls Jürchedei's two services, the arrow-shot that wounded Senggum and the trapping of Jaqa Gambu, and gives him Ibaqa-Beki, with a command that her place be kept for descendants; he praises Qubilai, Jelme, Jebe and Sübegetei as his dogs, names four heroes who keep his heart at ease, and puts Qubilai in charge with Bedüün; and he names Qunan, 'wolf by night and crow by day', and Kökösös among the trusted four.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Žürčedej-e ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, to Jürchedei saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Jürchedei:
sentences.n: Shiratori's colon after ügülerün introduces the speech that follows. Čiṅgis Qaγan is a name plus title: Chinggis, qan. The dative -e on Žürčedej-e is written -je after the i (Ming 行, 'to'). ügülerün is ügüle- 'to speak' with the converb of time -rün, 'saying, when saying'.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Erkin tusa čin-u Kereid-lüġe Qara-Qalžid-Eled qadqulduqui-dur herüžü büküi-dür
sentences.l: "Important favour your, with the Kereid, at Qara-Qalžid-Eled, at the fighting, grieving, at the being,
sentences.i: “Your vital service: when we fought the Kereid at Qalaqaljid-Eled, and I was in anxiety,
sentences.n: This is where the speech to Jürchedei begins, and the Ming sets the scene: 'important favour of you', then a time clause. qadqulduqui-dur is the reciprocal participle 'the fighting each other' with the dative-locative -dur, 'at the time of' (Ming 厮殺時). herüžü büküi-dür is a converb chain: herü- 'to grieve' (Ming 愁着) + -žü, then bü- 'to be' + participle -küi + -dür, 'when being'. Shiratori prints the place as Qara-Qalžid-Eled (the Qara-Qalžid sands of §§170–171); `i` uses the form already published at §200 for the same sands, Qalaqaljid-Eled. The sentence does not say who grieves; I take it to be Chinggis (or all of them), and the Ming gives no help. The unit is cut here from the next because Shiratori's period comes only at aldaba-že; this is a break in one sentence. Shiratori's opening quotation mark is on Erkin, and it is the outer quote of the whole speech to Jürchedei; the matching close is at Tasultuγai, which also closes the inner speech to Ibaqa, so I close both marks there.

morph.gloss: the Kereid, a people [種名 一同]
Qalaqaljid-Eled (printed Qara-Qalžid-Eled here), the sands where the Kereid were fought; a place name (Ming: 地名) [地名]
dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]
to grieve, be anxious (stem inferred from the Ming) [愁着]
dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]

sentences.t: Quildar anda aman aldaba-že.
sentences.l: Quildar sworn-brother, mouth let-go indeed.
sentences.i: Quildar, the sworn brother, gave his word.
sentences.n: aman aldaba-že: aman is 'mouth' (Ming 口), alda- 'to let slip, let go' (Ming 開了, 'opened'; the stem is alda-, not ald-, since the past -ba follows directly); the pair is a set phrase, 'to let the mouth go', i.e. to give one's word (compare aman aldaž-; §182 has aman negegsen, 'opened his mouth first', with the same Ming 開). That is my reading; the Ming's literal 'opened the mouth' is looser. -že is the closing particle 'indeed' (Ming 也者︀). Who swore, and what, is not said in these words, and the next unit says only that Jürchedei did 'that business'. anda is 'sworn brother' (Ming 契合), and the original does not say whose, so `i` does not supply a possessive.

morph.gloss: mouth; with alda- 'to let the mouth go', to give one's word [口]
to let slip, let go (aman alda-, 'to give one's word'; compare aldaž-) [開了 也者︀]

sentences.t: Üile in-ü Žürčedei či üiledbe-že.
sentences.l: Business his, Jürchedei, you did indeed.
sentences.i: That task, Jürchedei, you carried out.
sentences.n: Üile 'business, task' (Ming 勾當) and in-ü 'his' (the third-person genitive set after its noun, Ming 他的): 'that business of his', i.e. what Quildar had pledged. üiledbe-že is üiled- 'to do' + past -be + -že. The reading that Jürchedei carried out what Quildar swore is inferred from the sentence order; the Ming gloss does not state it.

morph.gloss: his (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to do, perform (from üile 'deed') [做了也者︀]

sentences.t: Üiledürün Žürčedei či dobtulžu
sentences.l: Doing-when, Jürchedei you, charging,
sentences.i: When it came to the doing, Jürchedei, you charged,
sentences.n: Üiledürün is the converb of time of üiled- (the same verb as above): 'when (you) did, at the doing'. dobtulžu is dobtul- 'to charge' (Ming 衝着, 'striking against') + converb -žu. The long chain that follows is broken at Shiratori's commas into five readable units; it is one sentence in the original, ending at negegdebe-že.

morph.gloss: to charge, gallop at (Ming 衝 'charge') [衝着]

sentences.t: Žirgin-i, Tübegen-i, Doṅγaid-i, Quri-Šilemün-i miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i erkid čeriġüd-i bügüde-ji daružu
sentences.l: the Jirgin, Tübegen, Dongqaid, Quri-Šilemün [each object], thousand bodyguards [object], the powerful (no case ending), the troops [object], all [object], overcoming,
sentences.i: overcoming the Jirgin, the Tübegen, the Dongqaid, Qori-Shilemün, the Thousand Guards, the leading troops, all of them,
sentences.n: Four names with the accusative -i (Ming 行, which is the Ming's mark of the object) and Shiratori's commas. Quri-Šilemün is very probably the Qori-Šilemün-Taiži of §§170–171, lord of Wang Qan's Thousand Guards (Shiratori prints Qori there and Quri here); `i` uses the published Qori-Shilemün and Thousand Guards. Tübegen-i the Ming glosses 姓(名)行 as for the others, and I take it as the Tübegen clan; Quri-Šilemün the Ming marks 人名行, a man. miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i is 'the Thousand Guards': turγaγ̇ (Ming 護衞) + plural -d + -i. erkid čeriġüd-i is 'the leading troops' (as at §153, erkid irge, 'the leading people'; erkid carries no case ending, so I take it as modifying čeriġüd-i rather than as a separate object): erke (stem uncertain) + -d plural (Ming 緊要每) and čerig + -üd + -i. bügüde-ji 'all (as object)'. The head verb is daružu 'overcoming', daru- + -žu.

morph.gloss: Quri-Šilemün = Qori-Shilemün (the Qori-Šilemün-Taiži of §170, probably), a man's name [人名行]
accusative, after a vowel: marks the object [行]

sentences.t: jeke γol-dur kürčü
sentences.l: Great centre-at arriving,
sentences.i: arriving at the great centre,
sentences.n: γol-dur: the Ming glosses 中軍 行 'to the army's centre'; the earlier glossary has γol 'stream, ravine' as the other reading, but 'centre' is the sense here. kürčü is kür- 'to reach' with the converb -čü after r.

morph.gloss: centre, main body (Ming 中軍 'centre army') [中軍 行]
dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]

sentences.t: Seṅgüm-ün eṅgesge qačar učuma-γar qarbuγsan-u tula
sentences.l: Senggum's red cheek učuma-with having-shot, because,
sentences.i: because Senggum's ruddy cheek was shot with an uchuma arrow,
sentences.n: A causal clause: qarbuγsan-u tula is the participle 'of the one shot' with the postposition tula 'on account of' (Ming 上頭). učuma-γar: učuma (Ming 箭名, 'the name of an arrow') + the instrumental -γar. qarbu- is active ('to shoot'), so the participle is literally 'of (one's) having shot Senggum's red cheek with an uchuma'; the Ming has no actor, and from the context it was Jürchedei who shot, but the words themselves do not say it, so `i` turns the clause into a passive rather than name him. eṅgesge qačar is 'red cheek' (Ming 紅 腮).

morph.gloss: Senggum, son of Wang Qan [人名的]
učuma, a kind of arrow (Ming 箭名 'arrow name') [箭名(敎)]
to shoot an arrow [射了 的]
because of, on account of [上頭]

sentences.t: müṅke teṅgeri-de eġüden žiloγ̇a negegdebe-že.
sentences.l: Eternal Heaven-by door, rein, was opened indeed.
sentences.i: by eternal Heaven the door and the rein were opened.
sentences.n: teṅgeri-de is the dative-locative with a passive verb, 'by Heaven' (Ming 天 行). negegdebe-že is nege- 'to open' + passive -gde- + past -be + -že. eġüden žiloγ̇a: 'door' (Ming 門) and žiloγ̇a (Ming 牽胷, a horse's breast-strap or rein). I read it as a pair, 'door, rein', a figure for the way being opened for them; this is uncertain. It ends the long chain begun at Üiledürün.

morph.gloss: Heaven, the sky as a power [天 行]
rein, bridle (Ming 牽胷, a horse's breast-strap; uncertain) [牽胷]

sentences.t: Seṅgüm-i ese širqaγsan böġesü ambar maqa bolqun büleġei bida.
sentences.l: Senggum [object] not wounded if-be, how perhaps become there-was we.
sentences.i: Had Senggum not been wounded, what would have become of us?
sentences.n: A conditional: böġesü is bü- 'to be' + conditional -ġesü (Ming 有呵). ese širqaγsan is 'not wounded' (ese negates a past action). The second half is hard: ambar (Ming 怎生 'how'), maqa (Ming 莫不 'perhaps not'), bolqun (Ming 壞 or 做每; bol- 'become' with -qun), büleġei (past 'there was'), bida 'we'. I read it as 'what, perhaps, would have become of us?', a rhetorical question about what would have happened to the army. The Ming glosses bolqun here 做每, 'doing/becoming', not the 壞 'spoil' of the other place, so I do not press 'be undone'; the sense of bolqun is uncertain and the English is a guess at the Ming.

morph.gloss: to wound, hurt (stem inferred from the Ming 傷) [傷了]
perhaps, perhaps not (Ming 莫不) [莫不]
to become (here, 'what would have become of us'; Ming 做每 here, 壞 'spoil' elsewhere; uncertain) [做每]

sentences.t: Žürčedei-ji erkin jeke tusa tere bolba-že.
sentences.l: Jürchedei [object] important great favour that became indeed.
sentences.i: That was Jürchedei's vital and great service.
sentences.n: The Ming writes 行 after Žürčedei, and -ji is the accusative-type ending (hence '[object]' in `l`); the sense is 'as for Jürchedei', and `i` renders it possessively: 'for Jürchedei (it was) an important great favour'. tusa 'favour, service' (Ming 恩) and erkin jeke 'important, great'. tere bolba-že: 'that became, so it was'; bolba-že is bol- 'to become' + past + -že.

morph.gloss: accusative, after a vowel: marks the object [行]

sentences.t: Tere qaγačažu Qalqa huruγ̇u neġürün
sentences.l: That parting, Qalqa downstream moving-camp-when,
sentences.i: When we parted from there and moved camp down the Qalqa,
sentences.n: Qalqa here is a river (Ming 河名), not the 'shield' of the same spelling. huruγ̇u 'downstream, along' (Ming 順着). neġürün is neġü- 'to move camp' with the converb of time -rün (Ming 起時). tere qaγačažu 'that, separating' leaves out what we parted from; 'from there' is supplied. Break in a converb chain: this unit and the next are one sentence.

morph.gloss: to part from, separate from [離着]
the Qalqa, a river (Ming 河名 'river name') [河名]

sentences.t: Žürčedei-ji ündür aγ̇ula-jin nemüre metü sedkižü jabuqu büleġe bi.
sentences.l: Jürchedei [object] high mountain's shelter like thinking, going was I.
sentences.i: I went along thinking of Jürchedei as a shelter like a high mountain.
sentences.n: The Ming gives nemüre 'shelter, screen' (遮護) and metü 'like' (般): 'like the shelter of a high mountain' (ündür aγ̇ula-jin nemüre metü). sedkižü jabuqu büleġe is the converb 'thinking', the participle jabuqu (jabu- 'to go' + -qu) and the past 'was', i.e. 'was going about thinking'. The accusative -ji on Jürchedei (Ming 行) is the object of the thought.

morph.gloss: accusative, after a vowel: marks the object [行]
shelter, screen (Ming 遮護 'screen, shield') [遮護]

sentences.t: Tere odču Balžuna naγ̇ur usulara kürbe-že.
sentences.l: That going, Baljuna lake water-drinking reached indeed.
sentences.i: Going on, we reached Lake Baljuna and drank its water.
sentences.n: Balžuna is Baljuna (Ming 海子名 'name of a lake'), naγ̇ur 'lake'. usulara (Ming 飮水 'drinking water') is probably usula- 'to drink water' (from usun) with an ending -ra whose function I cannot give; I read it as a converb. kürbe-že is kür- 'to reach' + past + -že. The Baljuna covenant belongs here in history, but the sentence does not tell it and I add nothing.

morph.gloss: Baljuna, a lake (Ming 海子名 'lake name') [海︀子名]
to drink water (from usun 'water'; Ming 飮水) [飮水]

sentences.t: Žiči Balžuna naγ̇ur-ača morilarun Žürčedei-ji alginčilažu
sentences.l: But Baljuna lake-from, mounting-when, Jürchedei [object] vanguard-acting,
sentences.i: But when we rode out from Lake Baljuna, with Jürchedei as vanguard,
sentences.n: žiči 'but, yet' (Ming 郤). morilarun is mori(n) 'horse' + -la- (to ride) + the converb of time -run. alginčilažu: alginčila- (Ming 頭哨做, 'to act as the advance scout'), analysis uncertain; the accusative on Jürchedei makes him the object, 'having him act as vanguard'. A break in a long converb chain; the main verb is daγ̇uliba two units on.

morph.gloss: accusative, after a vowel: marks the object [行]
to act as vanguard, scout ahead (analysis uncertain; Ming 頭哨做) [敎頭哨着]

sentences.t: Kereid-tür morilažu teṅgeri γažar-a küčü nemegdežü
sentences.l: Kereid-against mounting, Heaven to Earth strength being-added,
sentences.i: riding against the Kereid, with strength added by Heaven and Earth,
sentences.n: Kereid-tür is 'among, against the Kereid' (dative-locative -tür). teṅgeri γažar-a küčü nemegdežü: 'Heaven, to earth, strength, being added'. The Ming glosses γažar-a as 地行 and nemegdežü as 被添助着 'being added and helped'. The sense, 'Heaven and Earth adding to our strength', is natural, though the case ending on γažar-a is ambiguous (it could be 'to the earth').

morph.gloss: to add (stem inferred from the Ming 添) [被添助着]

sentences.t: Kereid irge muqudγažu daγ̇uliba.
sentences.l: Kereid people wiping-out, seized.
sentences.i: we wiped out the Kereid people and took them.
sentences.n: Kereid irge: the Kereid (a people name, the -d probably a plural) and irge 'people' (Ming 百姓), a variant of irgen. muqudγažu daγ̇uliba: muqudγa- 'to wipe out' (Ming 窮極着 'to the extreme') + -žu, then daγ̇uli- 'to plunder, seize' + past -ba. The Ming sentence ends here with the Kereid 'seized'.

morph.gloss: to wipe out, destroy (stem likely; Ming 絕 'cut off') [敎窮極着]

sentences.t: Erkid ulus oṅžaldažu
sentences.l: The powerful ones' realm being-cut-off,
sentences.i: With the leading nation cut off,
sentences.n: Erkid ulus: the plural erke 'power' (Ming 緊要的每, 'the important ones'), so 'the leading nation' (compare erkid irge, 'the leading people', at §153). oṅžaldažu is a verb I cannot place (Ming 被斷絕着 'being cut off'); I give it as 'cut off', and the passive sense is the Ming's; because it is passive and Shiratori's period falls after daγ̇uliba, `i` joins it to the next unit ('With the … cut off, the Naiman and Merkid …') instead of hanging it on the previous subject. The case of Erkid is not marked, which is why `l` has no 'of'.

morph.gloss: erke = power, authority (stem uncertain) [緊要的每]
to be cut off, severed (stem inferred; the passive sense is the Ming's 被斷絕) [被斷絕着]

sentences.t: Naiman Merkid čirai-ban quγuražu baildun jadažu busaṅγaγdaba-že.
sentences.l: Naiman, Merkid, own-face breaking, battle-facing unable, scattered indeed.
sentences.i: the Naiman and Merkid lost countenance, could not form their line, and were scattered.
sentences.n: A sentence in three clauses, none of them with an explicit subject: Naiman, Merkid; čirai-ban quγuražu 'their own face breaking' (Ming 顏色自的行 折了着, 'face-broken', 'losing countenance'); baildun jadažu 'unable to form battle order' (baildu- is inferred from the Ming 對陣 'facing in battle array', jada- 'to be unable'); busaṅγaγdaba-že 'were scattered' (busaṅ- 'scatter' inferred from Ming 被潰散, the middle -γa- uncertain, -γda- passive, -ba, -že). The grammatical subject is plural and I take it as the two peoples.

morph.gloss: to break off, snap (stem inferred; Ming 折) [折了着]
to face in battle order (stem inferred; Ming 對陣) [對陣]
to scatter (stem inferred; Ming 潰散) [被潰散了也者︀]

sentences.t: Merkid Naiman-i busaṅqui Soγ̇or-tur
sentences.l: Merkid, Naiman [object] scattering, at the clash,
sentences.i: When the Merkid and the Naiman were scattered in the clash,
sentences.n: busaṅqui is the participle 'the scattering' of busaṅ-, and Soγ̇or-tur 'in the clash' (Ming 引闘 裏, 'in the lure-battle'). The Ming reads Soγ̇or as a fight, not a place, and §158 has soγ̇or-tur as 'in that clash'; I follow that and do not take it as a name. Naiman-i has the accusative -i (Ming 種名行) where I would expect a plain case; `i` simply joins the two peoples.

morph.gloss: soγ̇or = a clash, skirmish (compare §158, 'in that clash'; sense uncertain; Ming 引鬭 'lead on to fight') [引闘 裏]

sentences.t: Kereid-ün Žaqaγambu žirin ökid-ü-ġen šiltag(i)-jar öġer-ün qarijatan ulus(i)-jar-an tumtaγ-a aγsan ažuγ̇u-že.
sentences.l: Kereid's Jaqa Gambu, two daughters-own because-of, own dependents, people-with-own, whole, dwelling was indeed.
sentences.i: Jaqa Gambu of the Kereid, on account of his two daughters, had dwelt whole, with his own dependents and his own people.
sentences.n: Žaqaγambu is Jaqa Gambu; his two daughters (ökid-ü-ġen: ökin 'daughter', plural -d, reflexive-possessive -ġen 'his own', Ming 女子每自的行) and šiltag(i)-jar 'because of' (the instrumental -jar on šiltag 'cause, reason'; Shiratori's (i) is a linking vowel). öġer-ün qarijatan 'own dependents' (Ming 自己的 親屬的每) and ulus(i)-jar-an 'with his own people' (the instrumental plus reflexive -an). tumtaγ-a 'whole' (Ming 完全). aγsan ažuγ̇u-že, 'was one who dwelt', Ming 住的有來也者︀. The meaning is that he lived undivided with his household; the reference to the two daughters is mysterious and I leave it so.

morph.gloss: Jaqa Gambu, a man's name [人名]
reflexive-possessive 'one's own', with linking vowel [自的行]
cause, reason (Ming 緣故) [緣故 裏]
dependents, those attached to a man (formation uncertain; Ming 親屬的每) [親屬的每]
whole, entire (Ming 完全) [完全 行]
to be, to dwell [有來 也者︀]
past: 'there was, he was' (ending uncertain) [有來]

sentences.t: Nögöġe-te daisun bolun qaγačaγsan-i
sentences.l: Second-time enemy being, the separated [object]
sentences.i: Next, [him] who had turned enemy and broken away,
sentences.n: nögöġe-te 'second, next' (Ming 第二 行) is odd: it can mean 'a second time' or 'secondly'. daisun bolun 'becoming an enemy' (Ming 反做着, 'turning against'). qaγačaγsan-i is the participle with the accusative: 'the one who had parted'. The grammar is loose; I read the clause as describing Jaqa Gambu turning enemy and breaking away; the accusative -i is not matched by a verb in this unit, so `i` carries it as '[him]', and the verbs γardažu barižu in the unit after next take it up. Chain broken in three: this, the next, then barižu.

morph.gloss: to part from, separate from [分離了的行]

sentences.t: Žürčedei üdüžü arγa-bar Žaqaγambu-ji
sentences.l: Jürchedei luring, with-a-plan Jaqa Gambu [object],
sentences.i: Jürchedei lured, by a stratagem, Jaqa Gambu,
sentences.n: üdüžü is üdü- 'to lure' (stem uncertain; Ming 引誘着) + -žü. arγa-bar 'by means of a plan' (Ming 敎計策, 'by contrivance'). Žaqaγambu-ji: the name with the accusative. The verbs follow in the next unit (γardažu barižu), so the object stands alone here in `i`.

morph.gloss: accusative, after a vowel: marks the object [行]

sentences.t: qaγačan baraγsan-i γardažu barižu bütüġežüġü-že.
sentences.l: Separating, finished [object], hand-laying, seizing, completed indeed.
sentences.i: who had broken away and was finished; laying hands on him, he seized him, and it was accomplished.
sentences.n: qaγačan baraγsan-i: qaγača- 'to part' + converb -n, then bara- 'to be finished' (Ming 了的行) + participle + accusative: 'the one who had utterly parted'. γardažu barižu 'laying a hand on, seizing' (Ming 下手着 拿着). bütüġežüġü-že (Ming 完備了有來也者︀ 'completed') is a verb I can only analyse in part: bütü- 'to be whole' (stem inferred from the Ming), perhaps a causative -ġe-, and the past -žüġü with -že.

morph.gloss: to be finished, used up (Ming 了; uncertain) [了的行]
to lay a hand on [下手着]
to take hold of, seize [拿着]
to be complete, finished (stem inferred; Ming 完備) [完備了有來 也者︀]

sentences.t: Tere Žaqaγambu-jin ulus-i nögöġe-te ülüdgen talaba.
sentences.l: That Jaqa Gambu's people [object], again, utterly destroying, took-captive.
sentences.i: Next he utterly destroyed Jaqa Gambu's people and took them captive.
sentences.n: tere Žaqaγambu-jin ulus-i: 'that Jaqa Gambu's people' with the accusative. nögöġe-te 'secondly, next' as above (so `i` has 'Next' in both places). ülüdgen is ülüd- 'to destroy utterly' (Ming 殘滅) + causative -ge- (uncertain) + -n. talaba is tala- 'to plunder, take captive' (Ming 虜了) + -ba. The subject is again unstated; it is Jürchedei.

morph.gloss: to destroy utterly (Ming 盡絕 'cut off entirely') [殘滅]
to plunder, take captive (Ming 虜 'take captive') [虜︀了]

sentences.t: Žürčedei-jin nögöġe tusa in-ü ene bi-že.
sentences.l: Jürchedei's second favour, his, this is indeed.
sentences.i: This is Jürchedei's second service.
sentences.n: Žürčedei-jin nögöġe tusa 'Jürchedei's second favour'; in-ü 'his' (Ming 他的) is redundant after the genitive, a reinforcing pronoun set after its noun; ene bi-že 'this is indeed' (bi-že, Ming 有也者︀). So the sequence suggests that the first favour was the cheek-shot, the second the capture of Jaqa Gambu.

morph.gloss: his (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.t: Alalduqui üdür ami-jan öregsen-ü tula
sentences.l: The killing-each-other day, life-own put-forth because,
sentences.i: Because on the day of mutual slaughter you risked your own life,
sentences.n: Alalduqui is ala- 'to kill' + -ldu- + -qui, 'the killing one another'. ami-jan 'one's own life' (ami + the reflexive -jan, Ming 性命自的行). öregsen-ü is a participle in the genitive with tula: öre- (Ming 出着了 'put out, staked') seems to mean 'put forth, staked'. The subject is unstated; the reflexive 'own' points back to it, and I take it to be Jürchedei, who is being addressed.

morph.gloss: to put forth, expose (stem inferred; Ming 出 'put out') [出着了的]
because of, on account of [上頭]

sentences.t: üküldüküi üdür ölümleġsen-ü tula
sentences.l: The dying-together day, fought-to-the-death because,
sentences.i: because on the day of dying together you fought to the death,
sentences.n: üküldüküi 'the dying together' (ükü- 'to die', -ldü- reciprocal, -küi, Ming 死戰的) and ölümleġsen-ü tula, 'because of having fought to the death' (Ming 鏖戰了的 上頭). Both clauses are parallel and both end in tula; the main clause follows in the next unit.

morph.gloss: to fight to the death (Ming 鏖戰 'fight desperately'; stem inferred) [鏖戰(了)的]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Ibaγa-Beki-ji Žürčedei-(j)e sojurγažu ögürün Ibaγa-da ügülerün:
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan, Ibaqa-Beki [object], to Jürchedei, favouring, when giving, to Ibaqa saying:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, when he gave Ibaqa-Beki to Jürchedei as a favour, said to Ibaqa:
sentences.n: Ibaγa-Beki-ji is the object of ögürün 'when giving' (ög- 'to give' + converb of time); Žürčedei-(j)e is 'to Jürchedei', with the (j) in brackets as Shiratori prints it. sojurγažu 'showing favour' (Ming 恩賜着). Beki here the woman's title: a rank, not 'wife'. Ibaγa-da is the same woman, now addressed (Ming 夫人名 行 'to the lady named'). The first quotation mark is on the next unit.

morph.gloss: Ibaqa-Beki, a woman's name with title (Ming 女名 'woman's name') [女名 行]
accusative, after a vowel: marks the object [行]
Ibaqa, a woman's name (Ming 夫人名 'lady's name') [夫人名 行]

sentences.t: "Čima-ji ülige čeġeži čin-u ügeġüi
sentences.l: "You [object] dislike, bosom your none,
sentences.i: ‘Of you, there was no dislike in my heart,
sentences.n: Čima-ji is či 'you' on the oblique stem čima- with the accusative (Ming 你行). ülige is Ming 嫌 'dislike', and čeġeži čin-u ügeġüi, 'bosom your none' (Ming 胷懷 你的 無). I read the unit as 'there was no dislike (nor reproach) in my heart for you', taking čin-u (Ming 你的) as an objective genitive, 'regarding you', rather than 'your heart'; in `l` the words are kept in their order. This is a guess from the Ming; the word ülige is not otherwise known. Shiratori's second opening quotation mark is on Čima-ji: Chinggis now quotes his words to Ibaqa inside his speech, so `i` uses single marks for this inner speech.

morph.gloss: accusative on the oblique stem čima-: 'you' as object [行]

sentences.t: üžesküleṅ tala maγ̇ui ese keġebe-že bi.
sentences.l: Appearance, looks bad not said indeed I.
sentences.i: I never said that your looks were bad.
sentences.n: üžesküleṅ (Ming 看像) and tala (Ming 容貌) are two words for 'appearance, looks'; maγ̇ui 'bad'. ese keġebe-že is 'did not say', ese negating a past form, and the closing bi 'I'. So Chinggis tells Ibaqa that he had no fault to find with her; the next sentences say why he gives her away.

morph.gloss: looks, appearance (Ming 看像; formation uncertain, from üže- 'to see') [看像]
looks, appearance, features (Ming 容貌) [容貌]

sentences.t: Ebür-tür köl-dür oroγsan žerge-dür žergelen baγ̇uγsan čima-ji
sentences.l: Lap-at, foot-at entered, rank-at in-a-row settled you [object]
sentences.i: You who came into my lap and to my feet, who settled in the row of rank,
sentences.n: Ebür-tür köl-dür oroγsan: 'having entered at the lap, at the foot' (Ming 懷裏 腳裏 入了的). žerge-dür žergelen baγ̇uγsan: 'having settled in the rank, in a row' (Ming 次序 裏 列着 下了的). The pair of images describes a wife in his household, in her place. Čima-ji 'you' (object) comes last, the head of the whole description.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]
row, rank, place in a line [次序 裏]
dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]
accusative on the oblique stem čima-: 'you' as object [你行]

sentences.t: Žürčedei-(j)e sojurγarun jeke töre sedkižü
sentences.l: Jürchedei-to favouring-when, great right thinking,
sentences.i: when granting you to Jürchedei as a favour, thinking on the great right,
sentences.n: Žürčedei-(j)e sojurγarun: 'when favouring to Jürchedei' (sojurγa- + -run, Ming 恩賜時). jeke töre, 'great principle' (Ming 大 道理); töre means rule, right order, and the Ming 道理 is 'reason'. sedkižü 'thinking' (sedki- + -žü). Here the chain begins that explains why he gives her; it is broken in three after this unit.

morph.gloss: rule, principle, what is right (Ming 道理 'reason, principle') [道理]

sentences.t: Žürčedei-jin qadqulduγ̇an üdür qalqa boluγsan-u daisun küġün-dür dalda boluγsan-u
sentences.l: Jürchedei's fighting day, shield having-become, enemy among cover having-become,
sentences.i: who on the day of battle became a shield and a screen against the enemy,
sentences.n: Two parallel participles in the genitive, each qualifying tusas-un below: qalqa boluγsan-u 'of having become a shield' (qalqa, Ming 㒀牌) and daisun küġün-dür dalda boluγsan-u, 'of having been a cover among enemy men' (Ming 敵 人裏 遮護 做了的). The Ming spells the shield as a plain word here, a figure for protection. qadqulduγ̇an üdür is 'the fighting day'.

morph.gloss: to fight (stem read from the Ming) [厮殺︀的]
dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]

sentences.t: qaγačaγsan ulus qamtudγaγsan-u butaraγsan ulus büküdgeldügsen
sentences.l: Parted people uniting, scattered people gathering-all,
sentences.i: who made the parted people one and gathered the scattered people whole,
sentences.n: qaγačaγsan ulus qamtudγaγsan-u (qamtudγa- as in the published qamtudγaba): 'of having united the people who had parted' (Ming 分離了的 百姓 敎相合了的). butaraγsan ulus büküdgeldügsen: 'the people who scattered', and büküdgeldügsen (Ming 全完了的) 'having made altogether whole', the stem büküdgel- inferred from bükü 'whole'. The genitive on qamtudγaγsan-u and the bare büküdgeldügsen are as printed.

morph.gloss: to join together, unite (from qamtu 'together'; causative sense, Ming 敎相合 'cause to unite') [敎相合了 的]
to complete, bring all together (stem inferred from bükü 'whole'; Ming 全完) [全完了的]

sentences.t: tusas-un in-ü töre sedkižü čima-ji ögbe.
sentences.l: Services' his principle thinking, you gave.
sentences.i: thinking on the right of his services, I gave you.
sentences.n: tusas-un in-ü töre: 'of the services, his right'. tusa 'service' with plural -s and genitive -un (Ming 恩每的). sedkižü čima-ji ögbe is 'thinking, gave you'. So Chinggis explains: because of Jürchedei's deeds I give you to him. The sentence is the second of a long chain; its end is broken here.

morph.gloss: his (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
rule, principle, what is right [道理]
accusative on the oblique stem čima-: 'you' as object [你行]

sentences.t: Mönö qoina min-u uruγ bidan-u oro saγ̇užu ene metü tusa kigsen töre sedkižü
sentences.l: Hereafter, my descendants, our place sitting, this-like favour done principle thinking,
sentences.i: From now on, my descendants who sit in our place should think on the right of services such as these,
sentences.n: Mönö qoina: the Ming gives 久 後 'a long time after' here, and the earlier glossary has 明 後; I take it 'hereafter, from now on'. min-u uruγ 'my offspring', bidan-u oro 'our place' (bida in the genitive; the Ming has 俺的 here). saγ̇užu 'sitting'. ene metü tusa kigsen töre: 'such a favour done, the principle (of it)'. The sentence is a request; the verb is implied by the unit below.

morph.gloss: hereafter; with qoina, 'from now on' (Ming 久 'long') [久]
my (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
our (bida, genitive stem bidan-, + -u, set after its noun) [俺的]
place, seat, position (Ming 位子) [位子]

sentences.t: min-u üge buši ülü bolγan uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele Ibaγa-jin oro bu Tasultuγai"
sentences.l: My word otherwise not making, descendants' descendants-to until, Ibaqa's place do-not be-cut-off.
sentences.i: Do not make my word otherwise: down to the descendants of descendants, let Ibaqa's place not be cut off.’”
sentences.n: min-u üge buši ülü bolγan: 'my word otherwise not making' (bolγan, 'making', Ming 做). uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele 'down to the offspring of the offspring' (Ming 子子 子孫行 直到). Ibaγa-jin oro 'Ibaqa's place', bu tasultuγai: prohibitive bu + optative tasul-tuγai 'let it not be cut'. The closing quotation mark is Shiratori's, on Tasultuγai; it must close both the inner speech to Ibaqa and the outer one, so `i` has both marks.

morph.gloss: my (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
Ibaqa, a woman's name [夫人名 的]
to be cut off (Ming 斷) [斷了者︀]
optative: 'let it be, may it be' [者︀]

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he decreed.
sentences.n: keġen žarliγ bolba is the closing formula after a speech: keġe- 'to say' + -n (the converb that closes a quotation), žarliγ 'decree' (Ming 聖旨), bol- 'to become' + past. So 'saying (so), he made a decree'.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Ibaγa-da ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, to Ibaqa saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Ibaqa:
sentences.n: A second speech to Ibaqa. Quote opens on the next unit.

morph.gloss: Ibaqa, a woman's name [夫人名 行]

sentences.t: "Žaqaγambu ečige čin-u čima-da qojar žaγ̇ud inžes
sentences.l: "Jaqa Gambu father your, to you two hundreds dowry-attendants,
sentences.i: “Jaqa Gambu, your father, [gave] you two hundred dowry attendants,
sentences.n: Žaqaγambu ečige čin-u: 'Jaqa Gambu, father your'; čima-da qojar žaγ̇ud inžes, 'to you two hundreds (plural), dowry attendants'. inžes is inže 'servants given with a bride' (Ming 從嫁每) with plural -s; qojar follows or precedes what it counts. The verb is ögčü büleġe in the next unit; 'gave' is supplied here.

morph.gloss: dative-locative on the oblique stem čima-: 'to you' [你行]
dowry attendant, a person who comes along with a bride (Ming 從嫁) [從嫁(每)]

sentences.t: čima-da Ašiγ-Temür baγ̇urči Alčiγ baγ̇urči qojar ögčü büleġe.
sentences.l: to you, Ashiq-Temür cook, Alchiq cook, two, giving was.
sentences.i: and to you the two cooks, Ashiq-Temür and Alchiq; he had given them.
sentences.n: baγ̇urči is a 'cook, steward of the food' (Ming 厨子). qojar follows the pair: 'two'. ögčü büleġe is the converb 'giving' with the past 'was': 'he had been giving, had given'. The two lists are joined without 'and' in the original.

morph.gloss: dative-locative on the oblique stem čima-: 'to you' [你行]
cook, steward of the food [厨子]

sentences.t: Edöġe Uruγ̇ud irgen-dür či odorun gerijes(i)-jen
sentences.l: Now Uruqud people-among you going-when, keepsakes-own
sentences.i: Now, when you go among the Uruqud people, as your own keepsakes,
sentences.n: Edöġe 'now' (Ming 如今). irgen-dür 'among the people' and odorun 'when going' (od- + -orun). gerijes(i)-jen, 'own keepsakes' (gerije 'token to remember by', Ming 遺念, + plural -s + reflexive -jen). This is the first half of a request that runs to od 'go'.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]
keepsake, token to remember by (Ming 遺念 'memento') [遺念 自的行]

sentences.t: na-da inžes-eče-ġen Ašiγ-Temür baγ̇urči-jan nigen žaγ̇un-i ögčü od"
sentences.l: to me from own dowry-attendants, Ashiq-Temür cook-own, one hundred [object] giving, go!"
sentences.i: give me one hundred of your own dowry attendants and your own cook Ashiq-Temür, and go!”
sentences.n: na-da is bi 'I' on the stem na- with the dative-locative, 'to me' (Ming 我行). inžes-eče-ġen 'from one's own dowry attendants', ablative -eče + reflexive. Ašiγ-Temür baγ̇urči-jan is 'one's own cook Ashiq-Temür'. nigen žaγ̇un-i is 'one hundred' with the accusative. ögčü od 'giving, go!' (the imperative od). It is addressed to Ibaqa and the Ming runs the objects together; I take the one hundred as being of the dowry attendants and the cook as a separate item.

morph.gloss: I (stem na- before case endings) [我行]

sentences.t: keġežü abuγ̇a.
sentences.l: Saying, took.
sentences.i: So saying, he took them.
sentences.n: keġežü abuγ̇a: 'saying, took' (Ming 說着 要了). abu- 'to take, ask for' with a past in -γ̇a that I do not otherwise know. So Chinggis took the cook and a hundred of the dowry attendants for himself.

morph.gloss: to take, ask for (Ming 要) [要了]

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Žürčedej-e ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, to Jürchedei saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Jürchedei:
sentences.n: The speech to Jürchedei follows.

sentences.t: "Ibaγa-ji-jan čima-da ögbe.
sentences.l: "Ibaqa [object]-own, to you gave indeed.
sentences.i: “I have given you your own Ibaqa.
sentences.n: Ibaγa-ji-jan is the name with the accusative -ji and the reflexive -jan 'one's own' (Ming 夫人名自的行). čima-da ögbe: 'to you gave' (Ming 你行 與了). So 'your own Ibaqa' means the Ibaqa who is yours, the wife.

morph.gloss: Ibaqa, a woman's name [夫人名 自的行]
accusative, after a vowel: marks the object [行]
dative-locative on the oblique stem čima-: 'to you' [你行]

sentences.t: Dörben miṅγad Uruγ̇ud(i)-jan či medežü ülü-ü aqu či" keġen sojurγažu žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Four thousands, Uruqud-own, you managing, not-? be you?" saying, favouring, decree made.
sentences.i: Will you not have charge of the four thousand of your own Uruqud?” So he said, and, showing favour, issued a decree.
sentences.n: Dörben miṅγad: 'four thousands' (the plural -d on miṅγan). Uruγ̇ud(i)-jan 'one's own Uruqud'. medežü is mede- 'to know' with the Ming 管着 'having charge of'. ülü-ü aqu: a negative question: ülü 'not' + -ü (a question particle?, the Ming puts 麽 on the next word), a- 'to be' + -qu. So 'will you not be one who manages?'. keġen sojurγažu žarliγ bolba, the closing formula, kept in the same unit because Shiratori puts no stop between. The closing quotation mark is on the last či.

morph.gloss: the Uruqud, a people [種名 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own, with linking (i) [自的行]
to know; here 'to have charge of' (Ming 管) [管着]

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Qubilaj-a ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, to Qubilai saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Qubilai:
sentences.n: Qubilaj-a is Qubilai with the dative -a after the i (written -ja). The name is the same as the later Khubilai; here a warrior, not the emperor. Section 209 begins.

sentences.t: "Küčütü-jin ġüžüġün bökö-jin bögse daružu ögbe-že či.
sentences.l: "Strength-having's neck, wrestler's rump pressing-down, gave indeed you.
sentences.i: “You pressed down for me the neck of the strong and the rump of the wrestler.
sentences.n: Küčütü-jin ġüžüġün: 'the strength-having's neck' (küčü + possessive -tü, Ming 氣力有的); bökö-jin bögse 'the wrestler's rump' (Ming 力士的 臀). daružu ögbe-že is 'pressing down, gave'. The sentence is a compact, idiomatic one: pressing down the neck and the rump are images of overthrowing a champion. či is unmarked, so it is the subject ('you'), not the recipient (the recipient is marked čima-da / čima-ji elsewhere); ögbe after a converb I take as 'did for (me)', a benefactive use, and that is uncertain: the Ming 與了 is only 'gave', and a plain 'you gave (them up)' is the other possible reading.

morph.gloss: wrestler, strong man (Ming 力士) [力士 的]

sentences.t: Ede Qubilai, Želme, Žebe, Sübegetei
sentences.l: These Qubilai, Jelme, Jebe, Sübegetei,
sentences.i: These: Qubilai, Jelme, Jebe, Sübegetei,
sentences.n: Ede 'these' (plural of ene) and four names, with Shiratori's commas. The Ming marks each as 人名.

sentences.t: ta dörben noγas(i)-jan sedkigsen-dür žoriγ̇ulžu ileġesü kür keġegsen-dür
sentences.l: You four dogs-own thinking-at, pointing, if-sent, "Reach!" saying-at,
sentences.i: You four, my own dogs: when I thought of it and sent you out, directing you, and said, ‘Go to it!’,
sentences.n: ta is the polite plural 'you'; noγas(i)-jan, 'one's own dogs' (Ming 狗每自的行), a compliment: loyal dogs (so also §195, dörben noγais). sedkigsen-dür 'when thought' (participle + -dür, 'at the time of'). žoriγ̇ulžu 'having had pointed out' (žoriγ- 'to point', causative; Ming 敎指着). ileġesü is ile- 'to send' + the conditional -ġesü, 'if I sent' (Ming 敎去呵). kür keġegsen-dür: kür 'reach!' (Ming 到) and 'when said'. Both -dür clauses are time clauses.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]
to point out, aim at (Ming 指) [敎指着]
to reach, arrive (bare stem; force uncertain) [到]
dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]

sentences.t: gürü kemkelün qal keġegsen-dür qada qaγalun
sentences.l: Rock smashing, "Qal" saying-at, cliff breaking,
sentences.i: you smashed the rock; when I said ‘Qal’, you broke the cliff;
sentences.n: gürü kemkelün: gürü 'rock' (Ming 石) and kemkelün 'smashing' (kemkel-, inferred from Ming 撞碎, + converb -ün). qal keġegsen-dür: the word qal (Ming 惹) is not understood, perhaps a command or a particle; I leave it unrendered. qada qaγalun 'cliff, breaking open' (Ming 崖 撞破). The wording is parallel: each command is followed by what the dogs did.

morph.gloss: to smash (stem inferred; Ming 撞碎 'smash') [撞碎]
dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]
to break open (stem inferred; Ming 撞破 'smash open') [撞破]

sentences.t: čegen čilaγ̇un-i čeġülün čeġel usun-i nitulun aba-že ta.
sentences.l: Bright stone [object] crushing, deep water [object] cutting-off, were you.
sentences.i: you crushed the bright stones and cut off the deep waters; so you were.
sentences.n: čegen čilaγ̇un-i čeġülün: 'bright stone, crushing' (Ming 明 石行 碎); čeġel usun-i nitulun: 'deep water, cutting off' (Ming 深 水行 斷絕). The last verb aba-že is a- 'to be' + -ba + -že (Ming 有來也者︀). These last two images, crushing the stone and cutting off the water, are the strongest of the series: nothing could stand in front of these four.

morph.gloss: to crush (stem inferred; Ming 碎 'broken to bits') [碎]
to cut off (stem inferred; Ming 斷絕 'cut off') [斷絕]
to be, to dwell [有來 也者︀]

sentences.t: Qubilai, Želme, Žebe, Sübeġetei ta. dörben noγas(i)-jan žoriγsan γažar-a iležü.
sentences.l: Qubilai, Jelme, Jebe, Sübegetei, you; four dogs-own pointed land-to, sending.
sentences.i: Qubilai, Jelme, Jebe and Sübegetei: you, my four dogs, I send to the land pointed out.
sentences.n: The four names again, and ta 'you'. noγas(i)-jan žoriγsan γažar-a iležü is 'to the land that one's own dogs pointed out, sending' (Ming 狗每自的行 指來的 地行 敎去着). The grammar is loose: a participle žoriγsan without a clear subject, which `i` leaves unnamed; noγas(i)-jan carries the accusative (Ming 行), so the dogs are the ones sent, not the ones who point. Shiratori stops after ta and after iležü.

morph.gloss: to point out, aim at [指來的]

sentences.t: Boγ̇orču, Muqali, Boroγul, Čilaγ̇un-Baγ̇atur ede dörben külüġüd(i)-jen dergede-ġen aγ̇asu
sentences.l: Bo'orchu, Muqali, Boroqul, Chila'un-Ba'atur, these four heroes-own, presence-own, if-lives,
sentences.i: While these four heroes of mine, Bo'orchu, Muqali, Boroqul and Chila'un-Ba'atur, live at my side,
sentences.n: Names then ede dörben külüġüd(i)-jen 'these four own heroes' (külüg, Ming 傑, + plural -üd + reflexive -jen). dergede-ġen aγ̇asu: 'at one's own side, if (they) live' (dergede Ming 根前, a- 'to be, to live' + the conditional converb -γ̇asu). The sense of the condition is 'so long as, if they are alive'.

morph.gloss: Chila'un Ba'atur, a name with the title baγ̇atur 'hero' [人名 勇士]
hero, outstanding man (Ming 傑) [傑(每) 自的行]
side, presence (Ming 根前) [根前 自的行]

sentences.t: qadqulduγ̇an üdür boluγ̇asu Žürčedei, Quildar qojar-i Uruγ̇ud Moṅγud(i)-jar-an urida-γ̇an baiγ̇uluγ̇asu
sentences.l: Fighting day if-becomes, Jürchedei, Quildar the two [object], Uruqud, Mongqud-with-own, in-front-own if-set,
sentences.i: and if a day of battle comes, and I set Jürchedei and Quildar before me, with their own Uruqud and Mongqud,
sentences.n: qadqulduγ̇an üdür boluγ̇asu: 'if a fighting day becomes'. qojar-i takes the two names as 'the two' with the accusative. Uruγ̇ud Moṅγud(i)-jar-an 'with their own Uruqud, Mongqud' (the instrumental plus the reflexive; the Ming has 種名 on the peoples). urida-γ̇an 'in front, in one's own front'. baiγ̇uluγ̇asu: bai- 'to stand' + causative -γ̇ul- + the conditional -γ̇asu, 'if I cause to stand' (Ming 敎立呵). The dependent clauses of this unit and the one before build to the main clause below.

morph.gloss: the Mongqud, a people [種名 自的行]
before, in front [前面 自的行]

sentences.t: bügüde sedkil(i)-jen amuqu büleġe bi" keġebe.
sentences.l: all heart-own at-ease was I," said.
sentences.i: then my heart will be wholly at ease,” he said.
sentences.n: bügüde sedkil(i)-jen amuqu büleġe bi: 'all, one's own heart at ease, was I' (Ming 都 心自的行 安 有來 我). The Ming has a past 'was', but the sense is generalizing, 'would be'. amuqu is amu- 'to be at ease' + -qu. keġebe 'said'. The quotation ends with bi.

morph.gloss: to be at ease, rest (Ming 安) [安]

sentences.t: "Či Qubilai čerig-ün üile bügüde-ji aqalažu ülü-ü aqu" keġen sojurγažu žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: "You Qubilai, army's business all [object] heading, not-? be you?" saying, favouring, decree made.
sentences.i: “You, Qubilai: will you not take the lead over all the business of the army?” So he said, and, showing favour, issued a decree.
sentences.n: A second, shorter speech to Qubilai, with the opening mark Shiratori prints on Či. aqalažu is aqa 'elder' + -la- + -žu: 'being the elder, taking the lead' (Ming 爲長着). The question is built like the one to Jürchedei in the previous section: ülü-ü aqu. bügüde-ji 'all' is the object. The closing formula is kept with the speech because Shiratori puts no stop between.

morph.gloss: accusative, after a vowel: marks the object [行]

sentences.t: Basa Bedüġün-ü možirγaγ-un tula bi maγ̇uilažu jabužu miṅγan ese ögbe.
sentences.l: Again Bedüün's perverseness because-of, I vexed going, thousand not gave.
sentences.i: “Again, because of Bedüün's perversity, I was vexed and did not give him a thousand.
sentences.n: Bedüġün-ü možirγaγ-un tula: the name in the genitive, then možirγaγ (Ming 抝的 'twisted, obstinate') + -un, 'because of the crookedness'. maγ̇uilažu: maγ̇ui 'bad' + -la- (Ming 煩惱着 'being vexed') + -žu; jabužu 'going', so 'went about vexed'. miṅγan ese ögbe 'a thousand not gave'. The Ming's 'me' is the speaker, Chinggis. Shiratori prints no opening quotation mark here, but the first person (bi) and the address to Qubilai that follows show this is Chinggis speaking, in one speech with the next two units, which ends at jabuγdaqu"; I supply the opening mark in `i` (before Basa), not in `l`.

morph.gloss: crooked, perverse (Ming 抝的 'obstinate'; uncertain) [(抝的)]
because of, on account of [上頭]

sentences.t: Či ima-da žöb bi-že.
sentences.l: You him-to right indeed.
sentences.i: You are the right one for him.
sentences.n: ima-da 'to him' (Ming 他 行; the stem ima is uncertain). žöb 'right, proper' (Ming 正好) and bi-že 'is indeed'. So Chinggis tells Qubilai that the two will suit. The speech of which this is the second sentence opens in the previous unit (see there) and closes at jabuγdaqu".

sentences.t: Čima-luγ̇a minγalažu ejetüldüžü jabuγdaqu" keġebe.
sentences.l: With-you thousand-making, consulting-together, to-be-acted" said.
sentences.i: Forming a thousand with you and taking counsel together, [he] should proceed,” he said.
sentences.n: Čima-luγ̇a 'together with you' (či + oblique -ma- + the comitative -luγ̇a, Ming 一同). minγalažu 'making a thousand' (from miṅγan) and ejetüldüžü 'consulting together' (Ming 商量着), both converbs; jabuγdaqu is jabu- 'to go, act' + a passive -γda- + -qu (Ming 可行, 'it is fit to go'). The quotation ends with jabuγdaqu. I take the last verb as an impersonal 'it should proceed', since a passive has no agent. The speaker's 'you' is the Qubilai of the paragraph, and the unstated subject of the infinitive-like jabuγdaqu is Bedüün (the ima of the previous unit), so `i` supplies '[he]'; the sense is that Bedüün's thousand is to be joined with Qubilai's.

morph.gloss: to make a thousand (from miṅγan) [做千戶着]

sentences.t: Basa "Mönö qoina Bedüġün-i uqad-že bida" keġebe.
sentences.l: Again "Hereafter Bedüün [object] we shall-understand indeed" said.
sentences.i: And again he said: “From now on we shall know Bedüün.”
sentences.n: Basa 'again'; Mönö qoina 'hereafter'; Bedüġün-i uqad-že bida: 'Bedüün (accusative), understand-indeed, we' (Ming 人名行 省每也者 咱). uqad is uqa- 'to understand' with -d (a plural or hortative ending, uncertain); the sentence seems to say 'in time we shall see his measure'. The Ming's 咱 is the inclusive 'we'. keġebe 'said'.

morph.gloss: hereafter; with qoina, 'from now on' (Ming 明 'tomorrow') [明]
to understand, know [省每 也者︀]

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Genigedei Qunan-a ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, to Genigedei Qunan saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Qunan of the Genigedei:
sentences.n: Section 210. Genigedei is marked by the Ming as a people (種名), so 'Qunan of the Genigedei'; this fits the later Qunan Geniges(i)-jen. Qunan-a is the dative.

morph.gloss: the Genigedei, a people (Ming 種名) [種名]
Qunan, a man's name [人名 行]

sentences.t: "Ta Boγ̇orču, Muqali teriġüten nojad-ta Dodai, Doqolqu-tan čerbin-e
sentences.l: "You Bo'orchu, Muqali and-the-heads, to the noyans, Dodai, Doqolqu and-his-like, to the cherbi,
sentences.i: “To you, the noyans, Bo'orchu, Muqali and the others, and to Dodai, Doqolqu and the like, the cherbi:
sentences.n: ta 'you' (plural, polite). teriġüten is teriġü 'head' with a plural possessive -ten, 'those headed by' (Ming 等項, uncertain), nojad-ta is nojan 'lord' with plural -d and the dative (Ming 官人(每)行). Doqolqu-tan the same ending (Ming 人名 等). čerbin-e 'to the cherbi' (Ming 官名行, a court rank, here plural in force). Shiratori has no stop after čerbin-e; the colon in `i` is mine, to carry the address over to what follows.

morph.gloss: plural possessive: 'those having heads' (uncertain; Ming 等項 'and the rest')
Doqolqu, a man's name [人名 等]
plural possessive: 'Doqolqu and his like' (Ming 等 'and so on')
cherbi, a court rank (Ming 官名 'office name') [官名 行]

sentences.t: ene Qunan qara süni gendü čino gegeġen üdür qara keriġe bolžu
sentences.l: This Qunan, black night male wolf, bright day black crow, becoming,
sentences.i: This Qunan, who in the black night was a male wolf and in the bright day a black crow,
sentences.n: qara süni gendü čino: 'black night's male wolf' (Ming 黑 夜 雄 狼); gegeġen üdür qara keriġe: 'bright day's black crow' (Ming 明 日 黑 老鴉). bolžu 'becoming'. Shiratori gives no genitive (and `l` adds none) and I read the two phrases as 'at night a wolf, by day a crow', i.e. he is at home in any weather; this is a metaphor of the one who goes with the army. gendü is the Ming's 雄, 'male'.

sentences.t: neġüküi-dür ese ünžigsen ünžiküi-dür ese neġügsen
sentences.l: Moving-camp-at not stayed, staying-at not moved,
sentences.i: when we moved camp he did not stay behind, and when we halted he did not move on,
sentences.n: neġüküi-dür 'at the moving' (neġü- 'to move camp' + -küi + -dür), ese ünžigsen (ünži- Ming 住, 'to stay'), ünžiküi-dür 'at the staying', ese neġügsen (Ming 起了). So the meaning is that he kept pace with Chinggis in both. The Ming's order of verbs is the reverse of what 'move' and 'stay' make natural, so this is my reading.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]
dative-locative: at, in, at the time of [裏]

sentences.t: bosu küġün-lüġe buši niγ̇ur ese žübčigsen
sentences.l: Other people-with other face not agreed,
sentences.i: with other men he never made peace by turning a different face,
sentences.n: bosu küġün-lüġe 'with other men' (Ming 別 人 一同) and buši niγ̇ur 'another face'. ese žübčigsen: žübči- (Ming 安來的 'was at ease'), uncertain, perhaps 'to come to terms'. In this and the next unit niγ̇ur 'face' (Ming 面) is read literally, and whether there is an idiom behind buši niγ̇ur I do not know. žübči- here (Ming 安) may be the same verb as žübči- 'to join on' (Ming 續) of the glossary; if so the sense would be 'did not attach himself'. This is difficult.

morph.gloss: to be at ease, make peace (Ming 安; uncertain) [安來的]

sentences.t: öšitü küġün-lüġe öġere niγ̇ur ese žübčigsen
sentences.l: Enemy-having people-with different face not agreed.
sentences.i: with men of enmity he never made peace by turning a different face.
sentences.n: öšitü is perhaps öši 'enmity' (Ming 讐) + -tü, 'having enmity'. öġere niγ̇ur 'a different face', ese žübčigsen as above. The pattern of the two units is parallel, 'with others / with enemies', and the sense may be that Qunan never switched his allegiance, but that is my inference, not the Ming's.

morph.gloss: enmity, grudge (Ming 讐 'enemy, feud'; stem uncertain) [讐有的]
to be at ease, make peace (Ming 安) [安來的]

sentences.t: Qunan, Kökösös qojar-ača eje ügeġü bu üiledkün.
sentences.l: Qunan, Kökösös two-from counsel without do-not act.
sentences.i: Do not act without counsel from the two of them, Qunan and Kökösös.
sentences.n: Qunan, Kökösös qojar-ača: 'from the two, Qunan and Kökösös' (ablative, Ming 兩箇 行). eje ügeġü: 'counsel (Ming 商量) without'. bu üiledkün is the prohibition: bu 'do not' with üiled- 'to do' and a plural imperative -kün (Ming 做事您 'you do'). The speech is addressed to the noyans named above.

sentences.t: Qunan, Kökösös qojar-tur ejetüžü üiledkün" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Qunan, Kökösös two-in consulting, act" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: Act after consulting with the two of them, Qunan and Kökösös.” So he decreed.
sentences.n: qojar-tur 'among the two' (dative-locative), ejetüžü 'consulting' (Ming 商量着), üiledkün 'you act'. keġen žarliγ bolba as above. The speech ends with the quotation mark Shiratori prints on üiledkün.

morph.gloss: to consult, deliberate (stem inferred from the Ming 商量) [商量着]

sentences.t: köġüd-ün min-u aqa Žüči bi-že.
sentences.l: Of sons my eldest Jüchi is indeed.
sentences.i: “Among my sons the eldest is Jüchi.
sentences.n: köġüd-ün is köġün 'son' with plural -d and the genitive -ün, 'of the sons'. aqa is 'elder brother' (Ming 長) here 'eldest'. bi-že 'is indeed'. Shiratori prints no opening mark of this speech; I have supplied one in `i` only, and the closing mark is printed at boltuγai.

morph.gloss: my (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]

sentences.t: Qunan Geniges(i)-jen teriġüležü Žuči-jin doro tümen-ü nojan boltuγai"
sentences.l: Qunan, Genigesid-own heading, Jüchi's under, ten-thousand's noyan let-be"
sentences.i: Let Qunan, leading his own Genigesid, be a noyan of a ten-thousand under Jüchi.”
sentences.n: Geniges(i)-jen 'his own Genigesid' (Ming 種名自的行 'a people'). teriġüležü: teriġü 'head' + -le- + -žü, 'heading' (Ming 爲頭着). Žuči-jin doro 'under Jüchi' (Ming 子名的 下). tümen-ü nojan 'noyan of a ten-thousand' (tümen, Ming 萬戶). boltuγai is the optative: bol- + -tuγai 'let him be' (Ming 做者). A tümen is a unit of ten thousand men.

morph.gloss: the Genigesid, a people (Ming 種名) [種名 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own, with linking (i) [自的行]
ten thousand, a unit of ten thousand men [萬戶的]
optative: 'let it be, may it be' [者︀]

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he decreed.
sentences.n: keġen žarliγ bolba, the closing formula.

sentences.t: Qunan, Kökösös, Degei, Usun-Ebügen ede dörben üžegsen(i)-jen ülü niγ̇un sonosuγsan(i)-jan ülü qabčiγun büleġe.
sentences.l: Qunan, Kökösös, Degei, Usun-Ebügen, these four seen-own not hiding, heard-own not concealing were.
sentences.i: Qunan, Kökösös, Degei and Usun-Ebügen, these four, did not hide what they had seen nor conceal what they had heard.
sentences.n: Four names, ede dörben 'these four', then üžegsen(i)-jen 'what one has seen' (üže- 'to see' + -gsen + reflexive -jen, Ming 見來的自的行) with ülü niγ̇un (Ming 不 隱諱, 'not hiding'), and sonosuγsan(i)-jan 'what one has heard' with ülü qabčiγun (Ming 不 藏匿每, 'not concealing'). niγ̇un I read as niγu- 'to hide' (as in the glossary) with the converb -n; qabčiγun is a verbal-looking form I cannot analyse (the -γun may be a participle), given from the Ming. büleġe 'were'. It is a character reference: these four report all they have seen and heard, hiding nothing.

morph.gloss: to see [見來的 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own, with linking (i) [自的行]
to hide (Ming 隱諱 'hide, conceal'; the stem is that of the glossary's niγu-) [隱諱]
converb: '…ing' (so 'not hiding'; ülü before a converb)
to hear [聽了的 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own, with linking (i) [自的行]
conceal, hide (Ming 藏匿每; formation uncertain) [藏匿每]

sentences.t: Ede dörben bi-že.
sentences.l: These four are indeed.
sentences.i: These are the four.
sentences.n: Ede dörben bi-že, 'these four, it is so' (Ming 這的每 四箇 有也者︀). It closes the list; Shiratori marks the end of the paragraph here.
